summary: BBN's traffic statistics for the ARPANET hosts for May 1973, as tables of packets output per host. It updates RFC 509.

eli5.summary: A monthly scoreboard of how many messages each computer on the early network sent.

questions: which host sent the most packets in may 1973
subtitle: BBN's May 1973 count of packets sent by each ARPANET Host, split into internode and intranode traffic.

tldr.problem: The network community wanted regular figures on how much traffic each Host put onto the ARPANET.
tldr.mechanism: A table lists, per Host, packets output within the same node (intranode) and to other nodes (internode), with totals and an average daily internode figure over 31 days.
tldr.outcome: Overall, 72055570 internode and 23587410 intranode packets were output, at 1.07 packets per message.

today: RFC 522 is a monthly statistics memo that updates RFC 509. Its metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: What the Report Is
sections.content: RFC 522, by A. McKenzie of BBN-NET and dated June 1973, attaches the Host traffic statistics for May 1973. It updates RFC 509 and is a data memo, not a protocol.
sections.eli5: A short cover note says: here are the numbers for last month.

sections.title: The Host Throughput Table
sections.content:
The table is titled Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output). For each site, such as UCLA, SRI or MIT, it lists each Host number with INTER-NODE packets (sent to other nodes), INTRA-NODE packets (kept within the node), and a TOTAL. A subtotal row sums the Hosts at a site and adds the average daily internode count and the number of days, 31 for every listed site.

IMP21, BELV, ABER and LBL are marked as having no traffic.
sections.eli5: Each row is one computer, with how many messages it sent to other places and how many it kept at home.

sections.title: What the Numbers Show
sections.content:
ISI HOST 1 had the most internode packets of any single Host, 12619260, with a daily average of 407073. AMEST HOST 2 followed with 8087860, and AMES HOST 0 had 7952957.

The totals at the bottom are 72055570 internode and 23587410 intranode packets. The daily average is 2324373 internode and 760884 intranode, and the average per node-day is 64566 and 21136. The ratio of packets to internode messages is given as 1.07.
sections.eli5: A few busy computers sent most of the messages, and the report adds everything up at the bottom.
